A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Hogwild! Inference and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Content can be matched across the relocation of inference benchmarks and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original reasoning and coding evaluations, cache and prompting ablations, collaboration scores, and GPU inference measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds extended-budget OlympiadBench evaluations and a comparison of human and LLM collaboration ratings on 100 generations.

M1.justification: Concurrent KV sharing, RoPE query rotations, cache layouts, collaboration prompts and answer extraction are retained. Appendix B elaborates implementation possibilities for previously suggested sequence parallelism without establishing a changed inference algorithm.

E1.justification: The GSM8k, LIMO, OlympiadBench, LiveCodeBench and AIME task coverage is retained. Longer reasoning budgets and human annotation of LIMO outputs extend settings and analysis without introducing a new task domain or represented population.

E2.justification: Sequential generation, Self-Consistency, Skeleton-of-Thought and FlashAttention comparisons retain their membership in corresponding experiments. The new extended-budget tables reuse the sequential baseline; the added Skeleton-of-Thought example introduces no new comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix E.3 adds QwQ-32B evaluations on OlympiadBench Math and Physics up to a 16,384 reasoning budget, extending the previous 8,192 range. Appendix G.4 adds a validation protocol using 100 manually rated LIMO generations. Existing benchmark splits and answer-generation limits are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds a robustness analysis for longer generations in Appendix E.3 and human validation of the collaboration metric in Appendix G.4. Existing cache-layout, prompting and worker-count ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix G.4 newly reports human–LLM rating correlation and statistical significance, r approximately 0.34 and p approximately 0.0005. Existing seed averaging, three-assessment judge averaging and latency quantiles are retained; the latency uncertainty display is relocated rather than newly introduced.

E6.justification: New Tables 3–4 report extended-budget results: at 16,384, Hogwild!/baseline scores are 75.26/74.81 for Math and 39.03/36.12 for Physics. Human-rating findings are added, while Section 4.3 removes the observation of no direct accuracy–collaborativeness correlation. Existing benchmark plots and inference-table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The RoPE dot-product identity, rotation-count and complexity reasoning, and cache definitions are retained. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the claims that existing reasoning models can collaborate through shared KV caches without fine-tuning or a fixed collaboration framework, enabling more efficient reasoning.

C2.justification: Appendix G.4 newly interprets human-rating agreement as evidence that the metric captures meaningful collaborative behavior. Appendix B adds the qualification that efficient sequence parallelism requires kernels overlapping communication and computation. Existing limitations concerning smaller models, longer contexts and the proprietary judge remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly specifies comparison of 4,096-token prefixes per worker; this documents an existing evaluation without establishing a rerun. Appendix B expands KV partitioning and communication details. Relocation of the inference benchmarks drops the explicit ten-GPU count, while hardware types and code/data access information remain.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds citations to Li et al. (2020), PyTorch Distributed, and Zheng et al. (2025), Parallel-R1, concerning distributed communication and parallel fine-tuning. The broader positioning against fixed collaboration frameworks is unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4.4 absorbs the former inference-benchmark appendix, with subsequent appendix renumbering. v4 adds several short subsections, a Skeleton-of-Thought example and implementation explanations, alongside limited copyediting, an affiliation edit and the NeurIPS conference footer. Most prose and the main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 3–4 and the human–LLM rating heatmap in Figure 20. v3 Figure 19 and Table 2 move into Section 4.4 as v4 Figure 8 and Table 2. Existing diagrams and plots are retained, with localized layout and pagination changes.

improvement.justification: The extended-budget results and human-rating comparison address limited gaps in v3's evidence about longer-generation behavior and collaboration-score validity. Added technical explanations also improve transparency. The modest human correlation and sparse annotation details limit the validation's strength, but the additions provide a supported overall gain while preserving the main evidence.
